headline: This law lets the Bureau of Indian Affairs check and improve sanitation, safety, and utilities on tribal fishing access lands along the Columbia River.
what_it_does: The law allows the Bureau of Indian Affairs to assess sanitation and safety conditions on federal land set aside for Columbia River Treaty tribes to reach traditional fishing grounds. The Bureau may sign contracts with tribes or tribal organizations to improve those conditions and to expand access to electricity, sewer, and water service on the land. The Government Accountability Office must later evaluate whether conditions have improved and report its findings.

who_it_affects.how: The tribe may work with the Bureau of Indian Affairs on contracts to improve sanitation, safety, and utilities on its fishing access land.

who_it_affects.how: Conditions at the sites may become cleaner, safer, and better connected to electricity, sewer, and water if contracts are carried out.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect on its enactment date of December 20, 2019, though the summary does not give specific deadlines for contracts or the Government Accountability Office report.
